Make a meaningful difference with UnitingCare Queensland 

At UnitingCare we are leaders in crisis response, the protection of vulnerable people and children, financial resilience, and family wellbeing. Our FaDS (Family and Disability Services) team work passionately across Queensland to make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

As a Local Service Manager, you'll be encouraged to grow, develop and feel empowered to make the everyday easier for the people we care so passionately about. Let's make a meaningful difference, together!

Your part in our UnitingCare team

We are currently seeking a Local Services Manager to join our Community Mental Health team based in Townsville. The Local Service Manager will provide line management and practice supervision, leadership and guidance to service delivery across several Community Mental Health programs.

There will be some travel involved to Brisbane, Agnes Waters and Cairns.

Key responsibilities of this role include:

Work within relevant quality and risk frameworks and guidelines in accordance with relevant standards to ensure delivery of high-quality services, respect of client's rights and confidentiality.

Manage programs within budget and in consultation with the State-wide Manager, contribute to the budget planning cycle with specified accountability requirements.

Manage and monitor client information systems ensuring case recording and client files are maintained to a high standard and reporting and assessments are completed withing allocated time frames.

Drive best practice standards and implement these within a quality assurance framework to enhance and strengthen the overall performance out outcomes of the services.

Lead a multidisciplinary team, provide supervision, build capacity and foster a positive high performing team culture

Hold a Tertiary Qualification (a bachelor's degree or higher) in a relevant field (e.g. Social Work, Behavioral Science, Psychology, Counselling, Social Science)

A lesser formal qualification with acquisition of considerable skills and extensive-diverse relevant experience to an equivalent standard (a minimum of 5 years or more).

Significant experience in providing services to children and families

Demonstrated experience in managing a team, financial oversight and compliance with quality standards along with an ability to provide quality supervision and training.

Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain collaborative partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.

Current Queensland Drivers licence.

Working with Children Check (Blue Card)

What makes a difference for you?

Flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance 

NFP Salary Packaging: Save tax and increase your take home pay by salary packaging your everyday living expenses and bills (up to $15,900) and meal entertainment (up to $2,650) per annum. To learn more about this benefit watch the video via the following link: Salary Packaging Explained 

A recognition and rewards platform, providing employee discounts at hundreds of retailers, including everyday expenses, holidays, health insurance, annual awards celebration, wellbeing and employee assistance programs 

12 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid partner leave, available after 6 months service, in addition to the government scheme 

Diversity and inclusive leave, offering paid gender affirmation leave and cultural leave options (paid and unpaid) for those who may celebrate Lunar New Year, Diwali, Ramadan, NAIDOC weeks and other significant cultural events 

Career development opportunities to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference 

A positive and inclusive team based on respect, shared standards, strong values and a commitment to serving others 

We'd love you to be part of our UnitingCare family 

Joining our FaDS, team, you'll also be welcomed as part of the UnitingCare family. The second-largest Queensland employer, we're a proud not-for-profit with more than 16,500 staff and 9,000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen's Hospital, and St Andrew's War Memorial Hospital, and have been leading by example for more than 100 years. 

Child safe, Child friendly 

UnitingCare is committed to being a Child Safe, Child Friendly organisation and will: 

provide welcoming, safe and nurturing services for children 

implement measures to prevent child abuse and neglect within our services 

appropriately and immediately address child abuse and neglect if it does occur 

abide by the Child Safe Standards and adhere to the Reportable Conduct Scheme 

Diversity & Inclusion 

Our approach is simple - everybody is welcome here. At UnitingCare, diversity is at the core of our who we are, our mission and our values. We are committed to providing equal opportunities to all employees no matter their sex, race, culture, sexual orientation, disability or gender identity. Demonstrating our commitment to reconciliation and building long-term employment opportunities for First Nations peoples, UnitingCare strongly encourages Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants for this position. 

Safe workplace 

We work hard to make our services welcoming and safe for every person. We are united in keeping children, young people and the elderly safe from harm, within our services, workplaces and the communities we support. We are committed to speaking up loudly for their safety. 

Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed in creating services and workplaces that are welcoming and safe for every person. We work together to protect children, young people, adults and the elderly from harm within our services and the communities we support. We speak up for their safety to ensure their voices are heard. - Skilled Reception Centre Manager wanted
- Full-time | 38 hours per week
- Join the team at The Greek Club & Convention Centre

About Us

The Greek Club & Convention Centre is a well-established hospitality and function venue in South Brisbane. The venue provides food, beverage and hospitality services for a range of functions, dining, banquets and special occasions.

\We are seeking an experienced and motivated Reception Centre Manager to manage the day-to-day operations of our reception centre. This role is responsible for overseeing hospitality service standards, food and beverage operations, staff management, venue resources, compliance, customer service and operational performance.

The Role

Reporting to senior management, the Reception Centre Manager will be responsible for the efficient daily operation of the reception centre’s food, beverage and hospitality operations.

The successful applicant will manage hospitality teams, oversee food and beverage service standards, prepare staff rosters, control operational resources and costs, maintain compliance requirements and ensure that customers receive a consistently high standard of service.

Key Responsibilities:
- Manage the day-to-day operations of the reception centre, including its food, beverage and hospitality operations.
- Oversee food and beverage service standards, ensuring service is delivered efficiently, professionally and in accordance with venue procedures.
- Lead, supervise, train and develop food and beverage attendants, supervisors and casual hospitality staff.
- Prepare staff rosters and allocate labour resources in accordance with operational requirements, service standards and labour-cost targets.
-Monitor staffing levels, performance, attendance and workplace conduct, and provide coaching and performance management where required.
- Ensure the reception centre is appropriately prepared, staffed and resourced to support the venue’s daily hospitality and function-service operations.
- Monitor the quality, timing and presentation of food and beverage service across the venue.
- Liaise with kitchen, bar, maintenance and other internal departments to ensure the smooth and efficient operation of the reception centre.
- Address customer enquiries, feedback and complaints promptly and professionally, and implement practical solutions to maintain service standards.
- Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety requirements, food safety standards, liquor-licensing obligations, responsible service of alcohol requirements and venue policies.
- Monitor stock levels, equipment and operational resources, and arrange replenishment or maintenance where required.
- Assist with preparing and managing departmental budgets, operating costs, labour costs, revenue targets and profitability objectives.
- Maintain operational records and prepare reports relating to staffing, service delivery, stock control, expenditure, customer feedback and venue performance.
- Identify and implement improvements to service standards, operational efficiency, customer satisfaction and team performance.
- Foster a positive, professional and collaborative workplace culture through effective leadership and communication.

Skills, Experience and Qualifications

To be considered for this role, applicants should have:
- A relevant qualification in Hospitality Management, Business Management or a closely related field and at least 1 year of relevant experience; or at least three years of full-time relevant management experience in hospitality, venue operations or food and beverage operations.
- Demonstrated experience managing hospitality operations within a club, hotel, convention centre, restaurant, function venue or similar establishment.
- Proven ability to manage food and beverage service operations, hospitality staff and day-to-day venue resources.
- Experience preparing staff rosters, managing labour costs, monitoring stock and controlling operational expenditure.
- Strong knowledge of customer-service standards, food and beverage operations, workplace health and safety, food safety and responsible service of alcohol requirements.
- Demonstrated experience supervising, training and developing hospitality teams.
- Strong organisational, communication, leadership and problem-solving skills.
- The ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced hospitality environment.

What We Offer:
- Competitive salary package between $75,000 - $85,000 plus superannuation.
- A full-time management role within a respected hospitality and function venue.
- Opportunity to lead and develop a professional hospitality team.
- Supportive and professional team environment.
- Ongoing professional development and career-growth opportunities.
